evidence: app/package.json:8-10 — hono ^4.13.14 is the current stable Hono release (v4.13.14, 2026-10-25); v5 exists only as 5.0.0-rc.1 and is untouched
app/src/app.js:20-25 — plain Hono core routing (app.get/use/notFound/onError) and stable serveStatic import; no middleware/helpers beyond these
app/src/views.js:1 — hono/html tagged template, stable since Hono 3.x
app/src/views.js:99-103,324 — only the five most basic htmx attributes (hx-get/hx-trigger/hx-target/hx-swap/hx-push-url); no extensions, no hx-on, no OOB swaps
app/public/app.js:3 — htmx:configRequest event, a long-stable public htmx event API
app/src/api.js:14-20 — standard Web fetch with in-memory promise caching; no cutting-edge platform APIs
reach.rationale: Every framework and platform API in use is long-stable and current-stable; the app deliberately stays on hono 4.x and htmx 2.x (both npm-latest, actively maintained lines) and uses zero experimental, preview, RC or canary features.

evidence: app/src/server.js:1-12 — server bootstrap isolated to a 12-line module using one stable serve() call
app/src/app.js:22-25 — all framework-middleware coupling (serveStatic mounts) confined to five lines in one file
app/src/views.js:1-8 — rendering isolated to a views module importing only stable helpers
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; even the framework-touching code is confined to thin seams (server.js, three serveStatic mounts, one views module), so any future API change would be a one-file swap.

evidence: app/package.json:8-10 — htmx 2.0.11 chosen over the newer htmx 4.0 (2026-08-28) which the authors keep off npm 'latest'; a conservative, justified pick
app/src/views.js:99-103 — htmx used only where it buys progressive enhancement (live search/filter swapping #results); server renders the same fragments (app/src/app.js:56-58)
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, and each stable API earns its place: htmx fragments implement the spec's live-filter/moves interactions with a plain-HTML fallback, and the Hono surface is the minimal stable core.

findings.issue: @hono/node-server pinned to ^1.19.0 (v1 line last released Apr 2026) while v2.0+ (Apr 2026, API-identical, 2.3x faster) is the current major and receives active security fixes, including the Sept 2026 serveStatic double-decode fix (GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f) that shipped in v2.1.3 but postdates 1.19.14
findings.suggestion: Bump to @hono/node-server ^2.x — the public API (serve, serveStatic) is unchanged per the v2.0.0 release notes, so the upgrade is low-risk and keeps the dependency on the security-maintained line. Current exact-path serveStatic mounts (app/src/app.js:22-25) make the exposure minimal regardless.

findings.issue: htmx 2.x (2.0.11) is used while htmx 4.0.0 was released 2026-08-28; 2.x remains npm 'latest' and maintained (2.0.11, 2026-09-22), so this is sound today but a future-migration consideration
findings.suggestion: No change needed now; note that htmx 2.x is a maintained line and track the 2.x → 4.x migration guide if the project later wants the fetch-based internals.

summary: The app is built entirely on long-stable, current-stable APIs: Hono 4.13 core, hono/html, @hono/node-server v1's serve/serveStatic, and htmx 2.x's five core attributes plus one standard event. It contains zero experimental, preview, RC or canary features and actively avoids both Hono 5 RC and htmx 4. The only currency note is a minor one: @hono/node-server sits one major behind on a stable-but-legacy line whose latest release predates a recent serveStatic security fix, though the app's exact-path mounts are not affected by that vulnerability.
